alerts.detail: Do NOT turn left at the top of Quicksilver — that's Boondoggle (black diamond), and beginners end up there. Warn at every unload for L1–L3 groups.
alerts.title: Beginner trap: Boondoggle at top of Quicksilver

alerts.detail: Skis steeper than its green rating. Often hosts junior races with large sections blocked off; looking uphill, the right side gets moguled up — keep beginners left. Check conditions before routing a group here.
alerts.title: Quicksilver trail: conditions layer required

alerts.detail: Almost never open to the public; used for CMAC and other club programs. Never route lesson groups here unless the group IS a club/race group.
alerts.title: Gold Hills: excluded from lesson routing

alerts.detail: K2 Face (black, gated B8) and upper-black terrain share the Forest Queen Express lift with the beginner pod. New instructors must know the unload-area layout and what is NOT their terrain.
alerts.title: Forest Queen unload: know what isn't your terrain

beginnerTerrainByLevel.levelName: Parallel on green/blue; edges, poles, turn shapes

dataModelNote: Gates are first-class records evaluated at plan time: skill-based, route-completion, safety/bailout (sidestep/sideslip doubles as a fallback branch the plan generator surfaces whenever a student is over-terrained), and awareness gates. Trail records need a conditions/alerts layer, not just static difficulty — how terrain skis is conditions-dependent.
familySlowZones: Around Tinkerbell / Quicksilver / Discovery lifts (Forest Queen base)

gates.requirement: No gate — this is where L1 starts.
Complete 2–3 top-to-bottom runs on the magic carpet + side step up the loading ramp.
gates.why: Carpet runs prove glide/stop/turn basics; the ramp side-step proves they can load safely. (David 2026-09-28)

gates.requirement: Sidestep down the steeper first ~50 yards of Discovery; bonus points for sideslip.
gates.why: Safety-lever gate: proves they can get down pitch too steep to turn on. Taught and gated here at Discovery, but it's the instructor's safety lever on ANY terrain — the plan generator should surface sidestep/sideslip as a fallback branch whenever a student is over-terrained. (David 2026-09-28)

gates.requirement: J-turns on Discovery (both directions) + linked wedge turns with turn shape controlling speed (solid L2).
gates.why: J-turns prove turn completion and stopping; route includes the Broadway traverse + a real run; speed control must come from turn shape, not stopping. (David 2026-09-28)

gates.liftOrTerrain: Forest Queen Express → Queens / Snow Garden
gates.requirement: Complete top-of-Chinook → Tinkerbell → Quicksilver merge back to base with no falls and minimal stopping.
gates.why: Queens run is much longer and more demanding though the pitch is easy — the gate is consistency/endurance on the shorter loop, not steeper terrain. (David 2026-09-28)

gates.requirement: L3: turn-shape speed control on greens without stopping between turns; briefed on the Boondoggle trap at unload.
gates.why: Last beginner step; unload area has the Boondoggle black-diamond trap; trail skis steeper than its color.

gates.requirement: Parallel on green terrain; stop and turn on demand on blue pitch.
gates.why: First-blue step. L4 blue list confirmed by David 2026-09-28 — all fine as listed; how each skis is conditions-dependent.

gates.requirement: Solid L4: comfortable parallel on other blues first.
gates.why: Finish steepens beyond typical blue pitch. (David 2026-09-28)

gates.requirement: L1–L3 groups: instructor knows the unload layout cold.
gates.why: K2 Face (black, B8 gate) and upper-black terrain share the lift; new instructors must know what is NOT their terrain.

liftProgression: Flatland — flat area at the base; very first steps on skis (L1)
Chinook Express → Tinkerbell via Broadway traverse (L2–L3)
Quicksilver chair → Quicksilver trail — LAST step; skis steeper than its rating (L3–L4)

steps: Exit the Chinook lift, do a U-turn.
Take Broadway (green traverse) toward the bottom of Forest Queen.
At the bottom of Forest Queen, turn left onto Tinkerbell.
Tinkerbell merges with the bottom of Quicksilver, back toward the base.
